title: GP solve allocation failure leaves caller outputs uninitialized
description:
ldlt_solve returns void on temporaryY allocation failure; callers consume output without a failure signal. Source-confirmed by independent core review; no OOM injection performed. Next: make failure explicit and add a focused allocator-failure regression.

Imported from .factory/findings/active/FND-20261023065605-60d4-repository-audit-010.json (category: functional, blocking: no).

outcome.summary: No defects found. Verified: ldlt_solve now returns bool and leaves X untouched on Y allocation failure; all five callers handle false. gp_infer_sd starts with gp_clear, so no state from an earlier inference survives; the three new failure branches (lines 835, 870, 886) free alpha/feature/fvt/S/loc/out/var and gp_chol (plus gp_chol_feat at 886) the same way as the existing allocation-failure branches next to them. gp_has_data stays false, the pointers stay NULL, ldlt_free sets L/D to NULL so no double free, and a gp_beta left half-written is unreachable without gp_has_data. gp_predict_projected on solve failure leaves mean = mixed*alpha, like the existing mixed_t/gamma failure branch, so the result is finite and defined. interp_peak_frequency skips interpolation when the solve fails. Test: built and ran it in the worktree (clang -O3, universal), 4/4 pass, no -Wall -Wextra warnings from the test or the GP source. Compiled the test against master's indigo_gp_guider.c with the bool-only case removed (that case cannot compile against the void API): all 3 behavioural cases fail at -O3 and -O0, so the test catches the defect. Stack poisoning only matters for detecting the old code; on the fixed code the result does not depend on uninitialized memory. The malloc macro comes after test_malloc and stdlib.h, so headers pulled in later only redirect indigo_safe_malloc, which is harmless. The Makefile rule matches test_star_detection. License header, English text and formatting match the neighbouring unit tests. The Xcode file reference is unique and sits in the unit test group with no .factory2 references. Non-blocking note: the gp_has_data-kept branch of inference_never_keeps_unsolved_results never runs on the fixed code; ASSERT_FALSE(g->gp_has_data) would be a stricter statement of the contract. Not verified: a Linux/GCC build of the test (the macro technique looks portable to glibc headers but was not compiled there), and leak-freedom (no ASan/leaks run). Other allocation si

No defects found. Part A: ldlt_solve returns false without touching X; all five callers handle it. The three gp_infer_sd failure paths free exactly what the neighbouring pre-existing branches free (alpha, feature, fvt, S, loc, out, var; gp_chol and, on the third path, gp_chol_feat through ldlt_free, which NULLs the pointers). gp_has_data stays false after gp_clear, so there is no leak, double free or dangling cache pointer. gp_predict_projected leaves mean = mixed*alpha (finite), the same as the existing mixed_t/gamma failure branch. interp_peak_frequency skips interpolation. Part B: ASSERT_FALSE(g->gp_has_data) after every injected failure; 11 of 11 failure points dropped, all three solve sites covered. Part C: all 12 sp/fr/timestamps/gear_error/variances/rt/rg/rv/detrend/windowed x2 sites converted; none of the excluded sites converted (grep). The removed NULL branches held only cleanup/return code made unreachable; no state reset was lost. The detrend hunk is a pure re-indentation under git diff -w; free(detrend) is still reached once. Sizes are unchanged and always >= 1 (count>=1, grid_size>=1, T>=2, n>=2, len>=1). Zero-fill is not observable. Every buffer is freed once on every path, including *spectrum/*frequencies hand-off. Use matches other indigo_libs callers. Test: built and ran 3x on macOS, all 4 cases pass, output identical across runs. No new warnings with -Wall -Wextra. No test path reaches an indigo_safe_malloc site, so no failure is injected into one. License header, Makefile rule, Xcode entry (unit test group, unique ID, no .factory2 refs) and git diff --check are clean. Limits: the old-code failure was not re-run by me (it relies on the owner note). Linux/Windows builds of the test were not verified. calloc sites (ldlt_factor) are not fault-injected by the test. Re-review of the final tree at 190d3de2c found no defects. The delta from 6c50530d4 is exactly 3 added lines in indigo_test/unit/test_gp_guider_alloc.c: a comment and #include <indigo/indigo_bus.h>, placed before #define malloc test_malloc. indigo_bus.h is include-guarded (indigo_bus_h), so the second include from indigo_gp_guider.c is skipped. Running clang -E on this file shows indigo_safe_malloc, indigo_safe_malloc_copy and indigo_safe_realloc now call the real malloc/realloc. An injected failure can therefore no longer abort, or exit(0), inside them. I built and ran the test twice on macOS: all 4 cases pass and the output is identical. Allocation counts are unchanged (11 for inference, 6 for prediction), and all 11 inference failures drop gp_has_data. git diff --check is clean, and formatting matches the file. Earlier findings carry over unchanged for indigo_gp_guider.c (ldlt_solve bool return, five callers, safe_malloc conversions, detrend pure re-indentation), Makefile and Xcode entry. Limits as before: I did not re-run the test against the old code myself (that rests on the owner note). Linux/Windows builds were not verified. calloc sites are not fault-injected.

history.text: Writing GP guider allocation-failure unit test

Reproduction (before fix): new indigo_test/unit/test_gp_guider_alloc.c, which compiles indigo_gp_guider.c with a malloc that fails the n-th call and 0xFF-fills other blocks, failed against the unfixed code: gp_infer_sd kept gp_has_data with a garbage alpha when the 6th of 11 allocations (the solve buffer) failed, gp_predict_projected returned NaN mean when its solve buffer failed, interp_peak_frequency returned NaN instead of the un-interpolated 2.0. After fix (ldlt_solve returns bool, all five callers handle false): all 4 cases pass and flow check (whitespace, unit) passes.
Building test_gp_guider_alloc against fixed and master gp_guider sources

Owner extended the scope after the first review pass. (1) In indigo_test/unit/test_gp_guider_alloc.c, inference_never_keeps_unsolved_results must assert that gp_has_data is false after every injected allocation failure (ASSERT_FALSE), instead of accepting kept data. (2) Audit and fix the remaining allocation sites in indigo_libs/indigo_gp_guider.c that this ticket had left alone (the malloc calls in the spectrum, regularisation, detrend and windowing helpers, originally reported near lines 406, 1054, 1093, 1149, 1298 and 1402); there use the framework allocator instead of plain malloc, as the rest of the framework does. The owner called it indigo_malloc; no such function exists, the framework helper is indigo_safe_malloc() from indigo_bus.h, which zero-fills and never returns NULL.
Applying owner additions: strict test, indigo_safe_malloc audit

Audit of remaining allocations in indigo_gp_guider.c: update_gp (timestamps/gear_error/variances, rt/rg/rv, detrend) and the two windowed buffers in estimate_period_length/estimate_extra_period were checked malloc calls with failure returns; converted to indigo_safe_malloc with the unreachable NULL branches removed (detrend block de-indented). calloc sites (compute_spectrum re/im, indigo_gp_guider_create g/buffer) already check and clean up, left unchanged; no unchecked-failure defect. Test inference_never_keeps_unsolved_results now asserts gp_has_data false after every injected failure. flow check (whitespace, unit) passed.

Correction to the audit: sp and fr in compute_spectrum were also plain malloc; converted to indigo_safe_malloc and the unreachable NULL branch removed (re/im calloc handling unchanged). Remaining plain malloc/calloc: ldlt_factor, ldlt_solve, gp_infer_sd, gp_predict_projected, FFT re/im calloc, indigo_gp_guider_create. flow check (whitespace, unit) passed.
Building and running test_gp_guider_alloc in the worktree

Owner approved the reviewer's optional suggestion: in indigo_test/unit/test_gp_guider_alloc.c include <indigo/indigo_bus.h> before '#define malloc test_malloc', so the inline indigo_safe_malloc() keeps using the real allocator and an injected failure can never abort or exit(0) inside it.
Including indigo_bus.h before the malloc override in the GP test
Reviewer relaunched for re-review of include delta
Preprocessing and running test_gp_guider_alloc on final tree
